newsitem.title: USA: Gasoline barge runs aground near Memphis.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline barge runs aground near Memphis.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard said Thursday that a gasoline barge ran aground Thursday morning 18 miles south of Memphis, closing traffic on the Mississippi for a 13 mile stretch.
The Coast Guard had no immediate information on whether any gasoline had been spilled into the river.
The barge is owned and operated by the Stapp Towing Co of Dickinson, Texas.

The M/V Shirley L. Stapp was the lead barge in a chain of barges carrying gasoline. It "ran aground on a dike at mile 717.2 on the lower Mississippi River," which is about 18 miles downstream of Memphis, Tenn., according to a Coast Guard statement.

"Coast Guard Marine Safety Office and Gulf Strike Team response personnel are on scene working closely with company representatives to minimize a potential major gasoline spill by off-loeading the damaged barge," the Coast Guard said.
